responses.reason: The corrected guarantees are sound. However, the hub must evaluate conversation grants and authorization, so 'no policy evaluation' is too broad.
responses.counter_proposal: Say 'the router performs no repository operation and evaluates no repository exposure policy.' Explicitly distinguish exposure policy from routing, authorization and admission controls.

responses.reason: This establishes an appropriate capability requirement, scope and lifecycle.
Accepted as a mandatory invariant across all diagnostic paths, including malformed requests and revoked capabilities.
The envelope preserves backend validation and addresses the important protocol-composition obligations.
The lifecycle design is acceptable. 'Only the hub holds the runtime credential' needs to acknowledge that tunnel-client must receive or independently obtain its runtime credential.
responses.counter_proposal: Say 'among repochat processes, only the hub handles the runtime credential; it supplies it securely to tunnel-client. Router and repository processes receive neither the credential nor credential-bearing inherited descriptors.'

responses.reason: A result already handed to tunnel-client may be buffered or in transit without having reached OpenAI. The proposed wording promises recall beyond the repository/router's control.
responses.counter_proposal: Define a revocation barrier: after acknowledgment, no old-generation result may be handed from repochat to the tunnel transport. Cancel work and discard queued results before that barrier. Document that results already handed to the transport may still arrive afterward and cannot be recalled.

responses.reason: Accepted. Use capability fingerprints rather than plaintext credentials as quota keys.
The separated adversaries and routing-only interpretation of socket hashes resolve the threat-model ambiguity.
Accepted as the release verification requirement, with additional binding-state tests described below.
Leaving the model-invoked approval tool out keeps the release focused. The local owner-operated grant command in D1 is a distinct mechanism.
The scope, sequencing, benchmark gate and deferred persistence are appropriate.

I accept the direction as prevention of automatic switching after initial binding, with explicitly approved multi-repository exceptions. I do not accept its current state lifecycle or the claim that the first repository necessarily reflects the capability the user pasted. The model still chooses the first request's capability. Expiry, eviction and rotation must also never silently turn an established conversation back into an unbound one.
responses.counter_proposal: Define L2 narrowly: 'After the initial binding, the conversation cannot access another repository without an explicit local owner grant.' Describe initial binding as the first successfully presented capability, regardless of its provenance. Make binding establishment atomic, preserve the restriction across expiry, rotation and hub restart, and make expired or forgotten bindings require explicit owner reauthorization rather than automatic rebinding. Scope identity by tunnel/profile and verified caller context where available; retain mandatory capabilities and fail closed on missing identity in required-binding mode. Approve D1 after the major issues below are resolved.

responses.reason: Capability-only fallback is an honest separate mode with L2 reduced, not solved. Shipping that fallback requires acknowledging that the owner's original all-three-losses requirement remains unmet; it must not be an automatic downgrade from required-binding mode.

new_issues.detail: Dropping bindings on capability rotation permits an old conversation to bind automatically to another repository. Expiry, bounded-table eviction and hub restart create the same bypass if absence means 'new conversation.' Preserving state only across router restarts is insufficient.
new_issues.proposed_change: Separate repository association from credential validity. Rotation revokes credentials and explicit grants without clearing the conversation's repository association. Expiry requires owner reauthorization. Persist the minimal association securely, or use an explicit owner-controlled enrollment mechanism after state loss. When capacity is exhausted, refuse new enrollment rather than evict restrictions and silently rebind.

new_issues.detail: Two concurrent first calls presenting different valid capabilities can both pass an unchecked 'unbound' test. Rotation or grant approval racing with dispatch can similarly admit an unauthorized generation.
new_issues.proposed_change: Use one authoritative atomic bind/check/admit operation before repository dispatch. Exactly one initial association wins. Bind authorization decisions and local grants to the current conversation, repository and credential generations, with revocation synchronized against admission.

new_issues.detail: The wire check establishes observed presence and stability, but not whether other callers can choose the same openai/session value. Session collisions or spoofing could transfer a conversation's explicit multi-repository grants. A branched chat retaining the same identifier would also inherit the association.
new_issues.proposed_change: Verify identifier separation and caller provenance, including deliberately conflicting metadata from another permitted client. Namespace bindings by tunnel/profile and available trusted caller identity. Do not treat a claimed subject field as authenticated merely because it exists. Document any identifier reuse as shared binding scope; if provenance cannot be established, describe binding as an accidental-switch guard rather than adversarial conversation isolation.

new_issues.detail: A short pairing phrase becomes a selector for an authorization change. Without precise request binding, retries, collisions, replay or stale requests could authorize a different conversation or credential generation than the owner intended.
new_issues.proposed_change: Generate phrases randomly, collision-check them against active requests, bound attempts, and make them single-use with short expiry. Bind each pending request immutably to the conversation, requesting identity scope, target repository and current generations. The target terminal must show the existing association and requested addition before explicit approval. Approval grants only that exact pending request; never a mutable 'latest request.'

new_issues.detail: The stated first-call residual attributes every initial mismatch to a user paste mistake. A model may instead choose another capability already present in repository-independent context, even when the user pasted the intended code correctly.
new_issues.proposed_change: Describe the residual as 'initial repository selection remains model-controlled.' If first-selection correctness becomes mandatory, require an owner-confirmed initial association outside model-controlled arguments.

remaining_disagreements: D1 must not automatically rebind after rotation, expiry, eviction or hub state loss.
Binding, grant checks and dispatch admission need atomic concurrency semantics.
Conversation metadata provenance and identifier scope need verification beyond presence and stability.
The local pairing mechanism needs immutable request binding and replay protection.
L2 must mean prevention of unapproved switching after initial association, rather than general proof of the user's intended repository.
summary: The capability, process and product-direction concessions are accepted, subject to three wording clarifications. D1 is the right additional guard, but major lifecycle, concurrency and grant-binding details remain. With those resolved, I would accept the narrower L2 guarantee and its initial-selection and explicitly authorized multi-repository residuals. D2 is an acceptable explicitly weaker fallback.
